ID-three-island-crossing.alt: The Snake River braiding around the islands at Three Island Crossing, seen from the overlook above the ford
ID-three-island-crossing.caption: The ford from the overlook — the Snake River running around the islands the crossing is named for.
ID-three-island-crossing.credit: Photograph: National Park Service staff, October 4, 2007 · Public domain (NPS image A-29)
ID-three-island-crossing.dateNote: A modern photograph of the historic ground. No emigrant-period photograph of this crossing is in the verified record; the oldest documented view lead is a BLM photograph from September 1987.

ID-city-of-rocks-california-trail.alt: Timothy O'Sullivan's 1868 albumen photograph of the granite rocks at City of Rocks, on its King Survey mount
ID-city-of-rocks-california-trail.caption: City of Rocks as the California Trail generation saw it — granite domes and boulders above the Raft River valley, 1868.
ID-city-of-rocks-california-trail.credit: Photograph: Timothy H. O'Sullivan, 1868, Geological Exploration of the Fortieth Parallel (Clarence King Survey) · Library of Congress — no known restrictions on publication
ID-city-of-rocks-california-trail.dateNote: An emigrant-era photograph of the real ground — among the earliest photographs ever made of this site.

ID-idaho-city.alt: Aerial view of Idaho City in 1925 — the town grid beside the dredge-worked creek flats
ID-idaho-city.caption: Idaho City from the air, 1925 — the whole town in one frame, and beside it the dredged creek flats that paid for it.
ID-idaho-city.credit: Photograph: Capt. A. W. Stevens, U.S. Army Air Corps, 1925 · University of Idaho, Archival Idaho Photograph Collection (archivalidaho357) — public domain

ID-craters-of-the-moon.alt: Big Cinder Butte rising beyond the lava fields at Craters of the Moon
ID-craters-of-the-moon.caption: Big Cinder Butte across the lava fields — the cinder country the monument was drawn around.
ID-craters-of-the-moon.credit: Photograph: National Park Service (NPGallery asset ac5d1d86) — public domain
ID-craters-of-the-moon.dateNote: Undated in the NPS catalog record.

st-joe-st-maries.alt: The 1910 firefighters' memorial plot at Woodlawn Cemetery in St. Maries — small grave markers ring a stone path around the central granite marker, under tall firs
st-joe-st-maries.caption: The firefighters' circle at Woodlawn Cemetery — the 1910 graves ring the path around the granite marker.
st-joe-st-maries.credit: Photograph: Ian Poellet, May 27, 2015 · CC BY-SA 4.0
st-joe-st-maries.dateNote: A modern photograph of the historic ground — the memorial plot as a visitor finds it today.
